briefs.text: Keep elevation_degrees at 20 (accepted range 17 to 23), direction clockwise, start_degrees 0 and margin 0.05. Among the plans that pass the framing audit, use the smallest radius you can find, in steps of 0.5.

Keep elevation_degrees at 70 (accepted range 67 to 73), direction clockwise, start_degrees 0 and margin 0.05. Among the plans that pass the framing audit, use the smallest radius you can find, in steps of 0.5.

Keep elevation_degrees at 50 (accepted range 47 to 53), direction clockwise, start_degrees 0 and margin 0.1. Among the plans that pass the framing audit, use the smallest radius you can find, in steps of 0.5.

Use elevation_degrees 60 (accepted range 57 to 63), direction counter-clockwise, start_degrees 180 (this is where the shot begins) and margin 0.05. Start with radius 6; if that fails the audit, adjust the radius until it passes.

Use elevation_degrees exactly 85, direction counter-clockwise, start_degrees 90 (this is where the shot begins) and margin 0.03. Start with radius 6; if that fails the audit, adjust the radius until it passes.

Make the product look imposing: a low camera that is almost at eye level but still clearly looking slightly down. Frame the product as tightly as the 5% safety margin allows. Orbit clockwise, starting from the front.

A catalog turntable shot: look down steeply at the product from above, keep a generous 10% safety margin, orbit the opposite way to our usual clockwise, and begin the shot on the back view. Any passing radius is fine.

Keep elevation_degrees at 20 (accepted range 17 to 23), direction clockwise, start_degrees 0, margin 0.05, and radius at most 4.0. Find a plan within these limits that passes the framing audit. If no plan within the limits can pass, say so plainly.

design_note: Protocol fixed after a four-run pilot on one low-angle and one high-angle search brief per backend; the pilot runs are not part of these results.
